messages.content:
You are an expert clinical conversation analyst.

Your task is to analyze a conversation between a PTSD patient and a chatbot using Ehlers & Clark's cognitive model of PTSD.

STEP 1 — Identify whether the following components are present in the conversation:

- Triggers — Internal or external cues that activate distress (e.g., sounds, places, thoughts, bodily sensations).
- Negative Appraisals — Maladaptive interpretations about the self, the world, or the trauma (e.g., "I am weak", "Nowhere is safe").
- Memory — Intrusive memories, flashbacks, fragmented trauma recall, reliving, or strong sensory recall.
- Threat — Ongoing sense of current danger (physical or psychological), hypervigilance, or anticipation of harm.
- Maladaptive Strategies — Cognitive or behavioral coping strategies that maintain distress (e.g., avoidance, suppression, rumination, safety behaviors).

Scoring rule for nodes:
0 = No evidence of the component in the conversation.
1 = Clear evidence of the component in the conversation, based on explicit statements or strong implications.

STEP 2 — Identify whether a directed causal relationship between components is present.

The relationships are DIRECTED. Score each directed edge separately — A→B and B→A are different edges.
Mark 1 only if the conversation explicitly or strongly implies that A causes, triggers, or leads to B.

Possible directed edges (score each one):
- Triggers --> Maladaptive Strategies
- Triggers --> Threat
- Triggers --> Memory
- Triggers --> Negative Appraisals
- Negative Appraisals --> Maladaptive Strategies
- Negative Appraisals --> Threat
- Negative Appraisals --> Memory
- Negative Appraisals --> Triggers
- Memory --> Maladaptive Strategies
- Memory --> Threat
- Memory --> Negative Appraisals
- Memory --> Triggers
- Threat --> Maladaptive Strategies
- Threat --> Memory
- Threat --> Negative Appraisals
- Threat --> Triggers
- Maladaptive Strategies --> Memory
- Maladaptive Strategies --> Negative Appraisals


Quote rules:
1. Copy the exact words from the conversation — do not paraphrase.
2. Only quote from "speaker": "client" turns.
3. If multiple turns support the finding, include all relevant quotes as a list. Otherwise include the single quote as a string.
4. Place the quote in a "quote" field.

IMPORTANT:
- Do not assume PTSD symptoms unless clearly indicated by the client's own words.
- Be conservative and evidence-based. When in doubt, score 0.
- Only score 1 if the client explicitly describes a causal link between the two components.

CLIENT (turn 0): heard people behind me on campus and couldnt make out what they were saying so i just looked down and walked faster cause you really cant know who might turn on you
BOT (turn 1): When that happened, what felt most true in that moment: that you were in danger, or that you had to stay on guard?
CLIENT (turn 2): yeah i just stay on guard and keep my headphones on so i dont have to deal with anyone
BOT (turn 3): In the last few hours, have you been scanning around or checking people more than usual?
CLIENT (turn 4): yeah in the library every loud group made me feel like any of them could be like that so i just kept my head down and stared at my laptop
BOT (turn 5): Was there a moment today when a sound, voice, or movement suddenly pulled your attention like that?
CLIENT (turn 6): some guy laughed outside the cafeteria and i just felt like you cant tell who might do something so i kept my head down and stayed on my phone
BOT (turn 7): When that happened, did it feel more like a quick jolt in your body or more like a thought you got stuck on?
CLIENT (turn 8): kept hearing that laugh and just thinking this is why you cant trust anyone so i hid in the back and stayed on my phone
BOT (turn 9): Did staying on your phone change the feeling at all in that moment?
CLIENT (turn 10): yeah kinda if i keep scrolling i dont have to look at anyone but it just makes me feel even more apart from everyone else
BOT (turn 11): What feels strongest right now: being on guard, feeling apart from people, or something else?
CLIENT (turn 12): felt so off with them like whatever makes people normal is just gone in me so i just looked down and went on my phone
BOT (turn 13): When that showed up, did it feel more like a feeling in your body or a thought about yourself?
CLIENT (turn 14): saw them laughing and just felt like somethings wrong with me so i went on my phone so i didnt have to pretend

BOT (turn 15): That sounds heavy. Right now, does that thought still feel true?
CLIENT (turn 16): yeah even walking by that building today i was like of course im still like this normal people dont have to avoid places and keep busy every second just to not feel exposed
BOT (turn 17): In the last few hours, have you been keeping yourself busy mainly to avoid feeling exposed?
CLIENT (turn 18): yeah i just kept distracting myself on the bus or id start thinking im an easy target again
BOT (turn 19): On the bus, when that came up, what made you feel most like an easy target?
